thesis: During periods of market stress, a surge in absolute volume momentum crossing above a floor of extreme order flow imbalance often precedes a reversal in sentiment, as measured by a normalized premium index crossing below a standardized acceleration of taker sell volume; this relationship suggests that panic-driven volume spikes, which temporarily overwhelm persistent selling pressure, create unsustainable conditions that trigger a mean-reversion in derivatives pricing and a deceleration in aggressive selling, revealing a pattern where extreme volume volatility acts as a leading exhaustion signal for bearish momentum.
